previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by chronic marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer and post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring continuous gastrostomy tube feeds was admitted for acute-on-chronic left upper quadrant abdominal pain localized near the G-tube site and worsened with tube feed infusion. Evaluation showed stable vital signs, reassuring abdominal exam without peritonitis, normal laboratory studies, and a chest radiograph without free air; there was no evidence of tube-site infection. Bariatric surgery recommended no additional imaging or surgical intervention, and the pain was felt most consistent with her known marginal ulcer and/or local tube-site irritation. She received IV analgesia initially, continued ulcer therapy with lansoprazole and sucralfate via tube, and tube feeds were restarted without difficulty to prevent hypoglycemia (supported with dextrose-containing IV fluids while feeds were off). Symptoms improved with pain control, and she was discharged home ambulatory with liquid oxycodone as needed and instructions to follow up with pain management and keep her planned end-of-month EGD.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ lady with history of ___ gastric bypass in ___ ___ 
complicated post-op course including post-bypass hypoglycemia 
requiring constant tube feeds via g-tube now admitted again with 
persistent pain at G-tube site. Patient's pain was managed with 
liquid oxycodone. CT scan showed no signs of misplacement, 
hemorrhage or infection. Patient's pain improved. Patient did 
experience asymptomatic hypotension in the setting of taking her 
atenolol. We stopped the atenolol and bolused fluids and the 
patient's blood pressure improved. The patient was kept on 
chronic tube feeds to prevent hypoglycemia. The patient will 
follow up with her PCP, ___ and General Surgeon. 

ACUTE PROBLEMS

# Pain at G-Tube Site:  
Pt. has long history of chronic pain at her gtube site. Her 
work-up this far during prior hospitalizations has been 
negative. There was concern on this admission for superficial 
skin infection at the site of G-tube insertion, but pt. had no 
systemic signs or symptoms of infection, no fevers, and no 
leukocytosis. Pt. underwent successful G-tube replacement on 
___, but unfortunately that failed to improve the pain. KUB 
w/o e/o perforation. It is likely that pain is most likely 
secondary to marginal ulcer as well as frequent manipulation of 
G-tube. It is possible that opioid-induced hyperalgesia is also 
playing a component.  Patient's pain improved throughout 
hospital stay. The patient was discharged on oxycodone and 
tylenol for pain management. 

# Hypotension
Likely secondary to atenolol in the setting of hypovolemia from 
her pain at the g-tube site. The patient responded well to 
fluids and was assymptomatic. The patient reports that her BP is 
often low and she stops her atenolol during these times. EKG 
showed sinus rhythm. Patient's atenolol was stopped. We 
recommended not restarting this medication as it may mask 
symptoms of hypoglycemia as an outpatient. 

CHRONIC ISSUES

# Post-Bypass Hypoglycemia:  
Managed currently with continuous tube feeding via G-tube. 
Continued q6hr FSG and continued tube feeds. 

# Marginal Ulcer: Known, chronic ulcer. Per prior notes, plan 
for EGD at the end of ___.  
- continue prevacid solutab and carafate  
- avoid NSAIDs  

# Depression: continued with home fluoxetine  
# GERD: continued with home lansoprazole  
# Anxiety: continued with home lorazepam  
# Insomnia: continued with home ambien

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
============================
- patient provided with 2 week supply of oxycodone (10mg 
q4hrs-84tablets)
- patient will need to followup with bariatric surgery/pain 
management for ongoing narcotic prescriptions
- we stopped patient's atenolol in the setting of hypotension; 
we recommend against the use of beta blockers in the setting of 
someone at risk of hypoglycemia as they would mask her symptoms 
if she were to become hypoglycemic at home
- patient will need to follow up with her PCP after discharge.

silhouette and well-aerated lungs which are clear. There is no focal

visualized. No free air is seen under the hemidiaphragms.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of free air.  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with severe pain at her g-tube site s/p
replacement // evaluation of G-tube ? abscess or hemorrhage around site.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through abdomen following
intravenous contrast administration with split bolus technique. Coronal and
sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS. Enteral contrast
was administered.

DOSE:  DLP: 439. 52 mGy-cm
IV Contrast: 130 mL Omnipaque

COMPARISON:  Abdominal CT scan dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST:

The visualized heart and lung bases are notable only for minimal dependent
atelectasis.

ABDOMEN:

A G-tube is in place with the balloon distended within the gastric fundus. 
There are ill-defined inflammatory changes within the left rectus abdominis
muscle at the site of G-tube insertion, without evidence of discrete
collection, hematoma, gas or abscess.

The patient has had Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. There is no evidence of bowel
obstruction or inflammation. The appendix is normal. There is no ascites,
pneumatosis or pneumoperitoneum.

The liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands, gallbladder and kidneys are
unremarkable. A duplicated renal collecting system is present bilaterally.
There is no hydronephrosis, but there is stable mild dilatation of the right
renal upper pole extrarenal pelvis.

The bones are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:


1. G-tube balloon inflated in gastric fundus with ill-defined inflammatory
changes in the left rectus abdominis muscle at the site of G-tube insertion.
No discrete collection, hematoma or abscess identified.
